translations.translatedText: # Monday 10.7.2017 (radio)

Finns want to stay in the EU. Japan's prime minister made a quick visit. The government got a new minister. Many young people have been bullied on the internet. The trees on the Esplanade in Helsinki must be cut down.
## The majority of Finns want to stay in the EU
![A bar chart](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9711115)
Open image viewer
Image: Taloustutkimus
Finns do not want a new referendum on Finland's EU membership.
In Yle's survey, over 70 percent of Finns think that a new EU referendum is not needed.
Over 60 percent also say that if a referendum were held now, they would vote for EU membership.
About 20 percent of Finns support a new EU vote. They also support Finland leaving the EU.
The majority of supporters of the Finns Party and the New Alternative group hope that Finland leaves the EU.
## Japan's prime minister popped in to Finland

![Japan's Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and President Sauli Niinistö shook hands at the Presidential Palace on Monday. On the right, Akie Abe.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9714515)
Open image viewer
Japan's Prime Minister Shinzō Abe greets President Sauli Niinistö. Photo: Jussi Nukari / Lehtikuva
Japan's Prime Minister Shinzō Abe has visited Finland.
President Sauli Niinistö and Mrs Jenni Haukio received Prime Minister Abe and Mrs Akie Abe at the Presidential Palace in the morning.
Niinistö and Abe discussed relations between Finland and Japan and many international questions, such as North Korea's missile tests.
Prime Minister Abe also congratulated Finland on its 100 years of independence.
Abe said that many Japanese people feel close to Finland, because Japanese children love Santa Claus and the Moomins.
## Annika Saarikko is the new Minister of Basic Services
![MP Annika Saarikko photographed in Parliament's Little Parliament on 27.06.2017](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9693872)
Open image viewer
Annika Saarikko of the Centre Party is the new Minister of Basic Services. Photo: Derrick Frilund / Yle
A new minister has joined the government.
Annika Saarikko of the Centre Party is the new Minister of Family Affairs and Basic Services.  Until now the job was done by Juha Rehula.
The change of minister was agreed already 2 years ago, when Prime Minister Juha Sipilä's government started.
## Online bullying is familiar to young people
![Work experience students in an illustration photo, an example of bad posture.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9505892)
Open image viewer
20 percent of young people say that they have been bullied online. Photo: Riika Raitio / Yle
Many young Finns have experienced bullying on the internet.

20 percent of lower secondary school-aged young people say that they have been bullied online. In addition, 40 percent say that someone else has published pictures or videos of them online that they themselves did not want published.
The information comes from a survey study done by Alma Media and the Foundation for Children and Youth.
## The Esplanade trees must be renewed
![The Esplanade park.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9712359)
Open image viewer
The trees in the Esplanade park are already old Photo: Kari Ahotupa / Yle
A big renovation will start in the Esplanade park in Helsinki in the coming years. The trees in the Esplanade park are going to be cut down.
The City of Helsinki says that the trees must be cut down because they are already old and rotten.  New trees will be planted in place of the old trees.
The work will start perhaps within 10 years. The city wants to tell about it already now, so that city residents have time to get used to the idea.
